statement: The last confirmed appearance of Homo erectus is a bone bed at Ngandong, Java, modeled via 52 radiometric age estimates (uranium-series on speleothems, luminescence and ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar on river terraces, and U-series/electron-spin-resonance on associated fossils) to 117,000-108,000 years ago — substantially overturning earlier, less rigorously dated claims of survival to as recently as ~27,000-53,000 years ago.

sources.citation: Rizal, Y., Westaway, K.E., Zaim, Y., et al. "Last appearance of Homo erectus at Ngandong, Java, 117,000-108,000 years ago." Nature 577: 381-385.
sources.author: Rizal et al.

does_not_demonstrate: that Homo erectus and Homo sapiens populations had direct contact in this region — the finding establishes temporal overlap at a continental/regional scale, not encounter
that Homo erectus persisted this late anywhere outside this specific Javan locality
